newsitem.title: UK: Four held in beating death of N.Ireland policeman.
newsitem.headline: Four held in beating death of N.Ireland policeman.

text.p: Four men were ordered held in custody on Wednesday charged with murdering an off-duty Northern Ireland police officer who was kicked to death by a mob.
One of the accused was the son of a part-time policeman, according to security sources.
The killing, blamed by media reports on pro-British Protestants, intensified tension in the province which has been shaken recently by rival guerrilla violence and sectarian bitterness.

During a brief court hearing in Coleraine, County Londonderry, a detective said they had replied "not guilty" when the charges were put to them. The magistrate ordered them held pending another hearing on June 20.

Gregory Taylor, 41, a father of three, was set upon in a street in the town of Ballymoney on Sunday by a mob angry that police had banned Protestant parades from passing through a nearby Catholic village, media reports said.

The policeman's killing, the latest in a series of street attacks by Protestant and Catholic gangs, has increased fears about the potential for violence during contentious pro-British parades over the next few weeks.
Northern Ireland's majority Protestants strongly support continued rule from London. The Catholic minority want an all-Ireland state ruled from Dublin.
